newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: FORECAST-Irish Life 1st half profits seen up.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Irish Life 1st half profits seen up.

text.p: Ireland's largest assurance group, Irish Life Plc, is expected to show an increase of about six to seven million punts in first half embedded value earnings, its key profit indicator, when it reports results on Thursday.

"I expect about 41 million punts embedded value earnings (EVE) in the first half," Riada stockbrokers analyst John Hogan told Reuters. "They will probably get the dividend up by about eight percent from 3.25 to 3.5 pence per share."

Embedded value earnings is a measure used by Irish Life to take into account the future value of policies sold during the year, the value of existing business and increases in shareholders' investments.
Merrill Lynch insurance analyst Roman Cizdyn is forecasting 40 million punts EVE compared with 34 million in the first half of 1995.
"I think new business should be picking up a bit in Ireland...and I think investment earnings will be quite respectable," Cizdyn said. "Those together will be the main driver."

Hogan said that, in the absence of something exceptional happening, profits should be split relatively evenly between the first and second halves of 1996, unlike 1995 where results were dragged down by a negative currency impact in the first half and boosted by a small currency gain in the second half.
"Last year Irish Life had a currency hit at the interim stage of something like seven or eight million punts due to a weak dollar," Hogan said. "They will probably be about line ball this time."
He said the group should also benefit from a benign first half in investment markets.
"I think in the first six months Irish Life's managed fund was up about just under eight percent compared to a rise of about five and a half percent in the first six months of 1995," Hogan said.
Analysts said Irish Life's U.S. unit, First Variable, appeared to be bedding down well and would compensate somewhat for a sluggish annuity business.
In June 1994 Irish Life bought First Variable Life Insurance Company, which is licensed to write variable annuity business in 47 states, for $51.1 million.
The group said at the time of the acquisition that First Variable's business allowed the group to reduce its overall dependence on the interest rate sensitive fixed annuity market.

"There has been a slowdown in the annuity business in the U.S. and that (First Variable) is hoped to make up losses with variable profits for which market conditions have been reasonable," one analyst said.
In the UK, analysts expected a favourable outturn given recent cost cutting.
"The UK will be doing well in profit terms because they have been cutting back a lot on costs so although the UK is winding down it will be quite profitable."
